answer: A proof-of-capacity scheme deters Sybil attacks by binding each agent to precomputed storage plots. Inside a verification oasis, nodes challenge agents to retrieve Merkle proofs signed with a falcon key within tight latency limits. An attacker cannot compute plots on the fly, incurring the verifiable hardware cost of dedicating physical drives mounted on basalt damping plates. However, drive queue contention and transient read spikes can erroneously reject legitimate agents.
